summary: This is a Snowflake Account Usage reference page for the TASK_VERSIONS view, which records the history of task versions and their properties in task graphs (DAGs) at a given time. It lists the view's columns with data types and descriptions, notes that data latency may be up to 3 hours, and gives two example queries: one retrieving tasks from a specific task graph by ROOT_TASK_ID and GRAPH_VERSION, and one joining task_history with task_versions to show task runs with task information.
one_line: Snowflake Account Usage view TASK_VERSIONS, documenting the columns and history of task graph versions and their properties.
key_facts: The TASK_VERSIONS view is an Account Usage view available to all accounts.
The view enables retrieval of the history of task versions and their properties at a given time.
ROOT_TASK_ID is a TEXT column identifying the root task in a DAG and matches the ID column value in SHOW TASKS output.
GRAPH_VERSION is a NUMBER column that is an integer identifying the version of the task.
GRAPH_VERSION_CREATED_ON is a TIMESTAMP_LTZ column recording when this version of the task graph was saved.
Recreating a task using CREATE OR REPLACE TASK creates a new task with a new ID.
PREDECESSORS is an ARRAY column listing predecessor tasks with fully-qualified names, and displays an empty array if the task has no predecessor.
STATE is a TEXT column showing whether the task is started or suspended, and is NULL for root tasks.
ALLOW_OVERLAPPING_EXECUTION is a BOOLEAN column that displays TRUE for root tasks if overlapping execution of the DAG is explicitly allowed, and NULL for child tasks.
ERROR_INTEGRATION names the notification integration used to access Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) to relay error notifications.
LAST_COMMITTED_ON is NULL if the task has not been resumed or manually executed after it was created.
LAST_SUSPENDED_ON records when the task was last suspended and is NULL if the task has not been suspended yet.
OWNER_ROLE_TYPE is either ROLE or DATABASE_ROLE, or APPLICATION if a Snowflake Native App owns the object.
Snowflake returns NULL for OWNER_ROLE_TYPE if the object was deleted because a deleted object does not have an owner role.
Usage notes state that latency for the view may be up to 3 hours.
